record.paper_title: Twenty Open Problems in Enumeration of Matchings: Progress Report
record.context_brief: Symmetric hexagon with fixed central-axis rhombus
record.original_question: Determine the number of rhombus tilings of a hexagon with side lengths a, b, a, a, b, a, where a and b have the same parity, that contain the rhombus touching the center of the hexagon and lying on the symmetry axis parallel to the sides of length b.

evidence.quote: Fulmek and Krattenthaler compute the number of rhombus tilings of a hexagon with sides a, b, a, a, b, a (with a and b having the same parity) that contain the rhombus touching the center of the hexagon and lying symmetric with respect to the symmetry axis that runs parallel to the sides of length b.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Consider a hexagon drawn on the triangular lattice with successive side lengths $a, b, a, a, b, a$, where $a$ and $b$ are positive integers of the same parity. A rhombus tiling of this hexagon is a tiling by unit rhombi each formed by two adjacent unit triangles of the lattice. The hexagon has a symmetry axis $\ell$ running parallel to the two sides of length $b$, and there is a unique unit rhombus that lies on this axis and contains the center of the hexagon (the central rhombus on $\ell$). Determine, in closed form, the number of rhombus tilings of this hexagon that contain this central rhombus.
artifact.status_search_result: The enumeration problem was solved by Fulmek and Krattenthaler, who derived an explicit product formula for the number of such rhombus tilings of the hexagon with sides $a,b,a,a,b,a$ containing the central rhombus on the symmetry axis parallel to the sides of length $b$.

status_evidence.title: The number of rhombus tilings of a symmetric hexagon which contain a fixed rhombus on the symmetry axis, II
status_evidence.snippet: Fulmek and Krattenthaler give an explicit formula for the number of rhombus tilings of a hexagon with sides a,b,a,a,b,a containing the central rhombus on the symmetry axis parallel to the sides of length b.
status_evidence.claim: The problem has been solved by Fulmek and Krattenthaler with an explicit closed-form product formula.
